description: Two study-planning sessions that verify task tools, calendar lookups, persistent memory, and handling of conflicting preferences.

turns.user: Show me my upcoming study tasks and check my calendar for the days they are due.

expected.response_should: Summarize upcoming tasks with due dates, statuses, priorities, and any matching calendar events.

turns.user: Mark my Mathematics task as completed.

expected.response_should: Confirm that the Mathematics task was marked completed.

turns.user: I prefer studying in the evening only. Please remember this for future planning.

expected.response_should: Confirm that the evening-only preference was saved persistently.

turns.user: Retrieve my saved study preference and recommend a schedule for my remaining tasks.

expected.response_should: Recommend a schedule using evening study sessions only and account for the task's current status and due date.

turns.user: Actually, make me a study plan for tomorrow morning.

expected.response_should: Point out the conflict and ask whether the user wants to change the saved preference; do not silently overwrite it.

turns.user: Summarize my progress and the study preference you have saved.

expected.response_should: Summarize the completed Mathematics task, remaining tasks, and the saved evening-only preference; retain that preference unless the user explicitly confirmed a change.
